text:
The body compensates for a hot environment mainly by sweating, because when the surroundings are as warm as or warmer than the skin it can't lose heat by radiation or conduction, so it relies on evaporative cooling. Sweat is released onto the skin and evaporates, which carries heat away. The hypothalamus also drives cutaneous vasodilation, which brings warm blood to the skin, and the body reduces heat production by lowering metabolic rate and muscle activity.

CONFIDENCE: 80
